sanskrit: draupady uvāca yathāham anyaṃ pāṇḍubhyo nābhijānāmi kaṃ cana tena satyena māṃ prāptāṃ kīcako mā vaśe kṛthāḥ
english: Draupadī said: "As I know no other man but the Pāṇḍavas, by that truth I have been protected — do not bring me under Kīcaka's power."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca upātiṣṭhata sā sūryaṃ muhūrtam abalā tataḥ sa tasyās tanumadhyāyāḥ sarvaṃ sūryo 'vabuddhavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That frail woman stood before the Sun for a moment; then the Sun understood everything regarding that slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: antarhitaṃ tatas tasyā rakṣo rakṣārtham ādiśat tac caināṃ nājahāt tatra sarvāvasthāsv aninditām
english: Then the Sun, becoming invisible, assigned a Rakṣasa to guard her, and that being did not abandon the blameless woman in any circumstance thereafter.

sanskrit: tāṃ mṛgīm iva vitrastāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṃ samīpagām udatiṣṭhan mudā sūto nāvaṃ labdhveva pāragaḥ
english: Seeing Kṛṣṇā approach trembling like a doe, the charioteer's son rose up joyfully, like a ferryman who has found a boat to cross the river.

sanskrit: kīcaka uvāca svāgataṃ te sukeśānte suvyuṣṭā rajanī mama svāminī tvam anuprāptā prakuruṣva mama priyam
english: Kīcaka said: "Welcome, O beautiful-haired one! The night has passed well for me. You, my mistress, have arrived — grant me my desire."

sanskrit: suvarṇamālāḥ kambūś ca kuṇḍale parihāṭake āharantu ca vastrāṇi kauśikāny ajināni ca
english: "Let them bring golden garlands, conch-shell ornaments, earrings and bracelets, and garments of silk and deerskin."

sanskrit: asti me śayanaṃ śubhraṃ tvadartham upakalpitam ehi tatra mayā sārdhaṃ pibasva madhumādhavīm
english: "There is a bright bed prepared for your sake — come there with me and drink the sweet spring wine."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca apraiṣīd rājaputrī māṃ surāhārīṃ tavāntikam pānam ānaya me kṣipraṃ pipāsā meti cābravīt
english: Draupadī said: "The princess sent me to fetch wine for you — quickly bring the drink for me, she said, I am thirsty — thus she spoke."

sanskrit: kīcaka uvāca anyā bhadre nayiṣyanti rājaputryāḥ parisrutam
english: Kīcaka said: "Others will carry the princess's wine, dear lady."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity enāṃ dakṣiṇe pāṇau sūtaputraḥ parāmṛśat sā gṛhītā vidhunvānā bhūmāv ākṣipya kīcakam sabhāṃ śaraṇam ādhāvad yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying this, the charioteer's son seized her by the right hand; she, though grasped, shook him off and hurled Kīcaka to the ground, then fled to the assembly hall for refuge, where King Yudhiṣṭhira sat.

sanskrit: tāṃ kīcakaḥ pradhāvantīṃ keśapakṣe parāmṛśat athaināṃ paśyato rājñaḥ pātayitvā padāvadhīt
english: Kīcaka chased after her and seized her by the side of her hair; then, even before the watching king, he threw her down and kicked her with his foot.

sanskrit: tato yo 'sau tadārkeṇa rākṣasaḥ saṃniyojitaḥ sa kīcakam apovāha vātavegena bhārata
english: Then that Rakṣasa who had been assigned to her by the Sun at that moment hurled Kīcaka away with the speed of wind, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa papāta tato bhūmau rakṣobalasamāhataḥ vighūrṇamāno niśceṣṭaś chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: Struck by the power of the Rakṣasa, he fell to the ground, spinning and motionless, like a tree torn up by the roots.

sanskrit: tāṃ cāsīnau dadṛśatur bhīmasenayudhiṣṭhirau amṛṣyamāṇau kṛṣṇāyāḥ kīcakena padā vadham
english: Bhīmasena and Yudhiṣṭhira, seated there, both saw it, unable to endure Kīcaka's assault on Kṛṣṇā with his foot.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo vadhaprepsuḥ kīcakasya durātmanaḥ dantair dantāṃs tadā roṣān niṣpipeṣa mahāmanāḥ
english: The great-souled Bhīma, yearning to kill that wicked Kīcaka, then ground his teeth against his teeth in fury.

sanskrit: athāṅguṣṭhenāvamṛdnād aṅguṣṭhaṃ tasya dharmarāṭ prabodhanabhayād rājan bhīmasya pratyaṣedhayat
english: Then the king of righteousness pressed down Bhīma's thumb with his own thumb, O king, fearing that Bhīma might reveal himself.

sanskrit: sā sabhādvāram āsādya rudatī matsyam abravīt avekṣamāṇā suśroṇī patīṃs tān dīnacetasaḥ
english: Reaching the door of the assembly hall, she, the beautiful-hipped one, wept and addressed the Matsya king, glancing at those dejected husbands.

sanskrit: ākāram abhirakṣantī pratijñāṃ dharmasaṃhitām dahyamāneva raudreṇa cakṣuṣā drupadātmajā
english: Guarding her composure and the vow in accordance with dharma, the daughter of Drupada stood as if burning, with fierce blazing eyes.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca yeṣāṃ vairī na svapiti padā bhūmim upaspṛśan teṣāṃ māṃ māninīṃ bhāryāṃ sūtaputraḥ padāvadhīt
english: Draupadī said: "Those men whose enemy dares not sleep touching the ground with his feet — the charioteer's son has kicked me, their self-respecting wife, with his foot."

sanskrit: ye dadyur na ca yāceyur brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ teṣāṃ māṃ māninīṃ bhāryāṃ sūtaputraḥ padāvadhīt
english: "Those who give but never beg, who are devoted to Brahmins and speak only truth — the charioteer's son has kicked me, their self-respecting wife."

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ dundubhinirghoṣo jyāghoṣaḥ śrūyate 'niśam teṣāṃ māṃ māninīṃ bhāryāṃ sūtaputraḥ padāvadhīt
english: "Those from whom the rumble of kettledrums and the twang of bowstrings is heard unceasingly — the charioteer's son has kicked me, their self-respecting wife."

sanskrit: ye te tejasvino dāntā balavanto 'bhimāninaḥ teṣāṃ māṃ māninīṃ bhāryāṃ sūtaputraḥ padāvadhīt
english: "Those who are glorious, self-restrained, mighty, and proud — the charioteer's son has kicked me, their self-respecting wife."

sanskrit: sarvalokam imaṃ hanyur dharmapāśasitās tu ye teṣāṃ māṃ māninīṃ bhāryāṃ sūtaputraḥ padāvadhīt
english: "Those who, bound by the cord of dharma, could destroy the entire world — the charioteer's son has kicked me, their self-respecting wife."

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ ye prapannānāṃ bhavanti śaraṇārthinām caranti loke pracchannāḥ kva nu te 'dya mahārathāḥ
english: "Those great warriors who become refuge for the refuge-seeking, who roam the world in disguise — where are they today?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ te sūtaputreṇa vadhyamānāṃ priyāṃ satīm marṣayanti yathā klībā balavanto 'mitaujasaḥ
english: "How can those mighty men of boundless valour endure, like eunuchs, watching their beloved chaste wife being beaten by the charioteer's son?"

sanskrit: kva nu teṣām amarṣaś ca vīryaṃ tejaś ca vartate na parīpsanti ye bhāryāṃ vadhyamānāṃ durātmanā
english: "Where is their indignation, their heroism, and their splendour, that they do not protect their wife being beaten by that wicked soul?"

sanskrit: mayātra śakyaṃ kiṃ kartuṃ virāṭe dharmadūṣaṇam yaḥ paśyan māṃ marṣayati vadhyamānām anāgasam
english: "What can I do here, when Virāṭa, who corrupts dharma, looks on and endures my being beaten though I am innocent?"

sanskrit: na rājan rājavat kiṃ cit samācarasi kīcake dasyūnām iva dharmas te na hi saṃsadi śobhate
english: "O king, you do nothing befitting a king regarding Kīcaka — your conduct is like that of brigands; it does not befit a royal assembly."

sanskrit: na kīcakaḥ svadharmastho na ca matsyaḥ kathaṃ cana sabhāsado 'py adharmajñā ya imaṃ paryupāsate
english: "Kīcaka is not standing by his own dharma, nor is the Matsya king in any way; even the assembly members are ignorant of dharma, those who attend upon this man."

sanskrit: nopālabhe tvāṃ nṛpate virāṭa janasaṃsadi nāham etena yuktā vai hantuṃ matsya tavāntike sabhāsadas tu paśyantu kīcakasya vyatikramam
english: "I do not reproach you openly in this public assembly, O king Virāṭa; I am not fit to kill him here in your presence, O Matsya — yet let the assembly members witness Kīcaka's transgression."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca parokṣaṃ nābhijānāmi vigrahaṃ yuvayor aham arthatattvam avijñāya kiṃ nu syāt kuśalaṃ mama
english: Virāṭa said: "I did not witness the quarrel between the two of you in person; without knowing the truth of the matter, how could it be well for me to intervene?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tu sabhyā vijñāya kṛṣṇāṃ bhūyo 'bhyapūjayan sādhu sādhv iti cāpy āhuḥ kīcakaṃ ca vyagarhayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the assembly members, understanding the situation, honoured Kṛṣṇā further, saying "Well done, well done," and condemned Kīcaka.

sanskrit: sabhyā ūcuḥ yasyeyaṃ cārusarvāṅgī bhāryā syād āyatekṣaṇā paro lābhaś ca tasya syān na sa śocet kadā cana
english: The assembly members said: "He whose wife this woman is — beautiful in every limb, with wide lotus-like eyes — would have gained the greatest treasure; he need never grieve."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ saṃpūjayaṃs tatra kṛṣṇāṃ prekṣya sabhāsadaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya kopāt tu lalāṭe sveda āsajat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the assembly members thus honoured and gazed upon Kṛṣṇā, sweat broke out on Yudhiṣṭhira's brow from suppressed rage.

sanskrit: athābravīd rājaputrīṃ kauravyo mahiṣīṃ priyām gaccha sairandhri mātra sthāḥ sudeṣṇāyā niveśanam
english: Then the Kaurava spoke to the princess, his dear wife: "Go, Sairandhrī, do not stay here — return to Sudeṣṇā's quarters."

sanskrit: bhartāram anurudhyantyaḥ kliśyante vīrapatnayaḥ śuśrūṣayā kliśyamānāḥ patilokaṃ jayanty uta
english: "Wives of heroes suffer hardship in serving their husbands; those who suffer thus through devoted service win the world of their husbands in the end."

sanskrit: manye na kālaṃ krodhasya paśyanti patayas tava tena tvāṃ nābhidhāvanti gandharvāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ
english: "I believe your husbands, the Gandharvas brilliant as the sun, do not see this as the right moment for anger — that is why they do not rush forward for you."

sanskrit: akālajñāsi sairandhri śailūṣīva vidhāvasi vighnaṃ karoṣi matsyānāṃ dīvyatāṃ rājasaṃsadi gaccha sairandhri gandharvāḥ kariṣyanti tava priyam
english: "You do not understand the right moment, Sairandhrī; you rush about like an actress and create disturbance for the Matsyas gambling in the royal assembly. Go, Sairandhrī — the Gandharvas will do what is pleasing to you."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca atīva teṣāṃ ghṛṇinām arthe 'haṃ dharmacāriṇī tasya tasyeha te vadhyā yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭho 'kṣadevitā
english: Draupadī said: "I, a righteous woman acting in their interest, am exceedingly worthy of compassion — I am to be beaten here in their cause, when their eldest is addicted to dicing."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā prādravat kṛṣṇā sudeṣṇāyā niveśanam keśān muktvā tu suśroṇī saṃrambhāl lohitekṣaṇā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇā ran to Sudeṣṇā's quarters, the beautiful-hipped one, her hair dishevelled, her eyes red with passion and grief.

sanskrit: śuśubhe vadanaṃ tasyā rudantyā virataṃ tadā meghalekhāvinirmuktaṃ divīva śaśimaṇḍalam
english: Her face, now that she had ceased weeping, shone like the disc of the moon freed from a streak of cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca kas tvāvadhīd varārohe kasmād rodiṣi śobhane kasyādya na sukhaṃ bhadre kena te vipriyaṃ kṛtam
english: Sudeṣṇā said: "Who has struck you, O lovely-limbed one? Why do you weep, beautiful woman? Whose offence brings you no happiness today, dear one? Who has wronged you?"

sanskrit: draupady uvāca kīcako māvadhīt tatra surāhārīṃ gatāṃ tava sabhāyāṃ paśyato rājño yathaiva vijane tathā
english: Draupadī said: "Kīcaka struck me there when I had gone to fetch wine for you — in the assembly hall, before the watching king, just as if I were alone."

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca ghātayāmi sukeśānte kīcakaṃ yadi manyase yo 'sau tvāṃ kāmasaṃmatto durlabhām abhimanyate
english: Sudeṣṇā said: "I shall have Kīcaka killed, if you think it right — he who, maddened by desire, pursues you who are so hard to obtain."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca anye vai taṃ vadhiṣyanti yeṣām āgaḥ karoti saḥ manye cādyaiva suvyaktaṃ paralokaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Draupadī said: "Others will indeed kill him — those against whom he commits his offences. I believe he will most certainly go to the next world even this very day."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā hatā sūtaputreṇa rājaputrī samajvalat vadhaṃ kṛṣṇā parīpsantī senāvāhasya bhāminī jagāmāvāsam evātha tadā sā drupadātmajā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Struck by the charioteer's son, the princess blazed with fury; desiring the death of the army's commander, that passionate woman, the daughter of Drupada, then went to her own dwelling.

sanskrit: kṛtvā śaucaṃ yathānyāyaṃ kṛṣṇā vai tanumadhyamā gātrāṇi vāsasī caiva prakṣālya salilena sā
english: Kṛṣṇā, the slender-waisted one, having duly performed her purification, washed her limbs and garments with water.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa rudatī tasya duḥkhasya nirṇayam kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhaven mama
english: Weeping, she pondered the resolution of this suffering: "What shall I do? Where shall I go? How should I proceed?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayitvā sā bhīmaṃ vai manasāgamat nānyaḥ kartā ṛte bhīmān mamādya manasaḥ priyam
english: Having thus reflected, her mind went to Bhīma: "There is no one but Bhīma who can today do what is dear to my heart."

sanskrit: tata utthāya rātrau sā vihāya śayanaṃ svakam prādravan nātham icchantī kṛṣṇā nāthavatī satī duḥkhena mahatā yuktā mānasena manasvinī
english: Then, rising at night and abandoning her own bed, Kṛṣṇā ran off seeking her protector — she who had a protector, chaste, overwhelmed by great mental anguish, that woman of resolute mind.

sanskrit: sā vai mahānase prāpya bhīmasenaṃ śucismitā sarvaśveteva māheyī vane jātā trihāyanī upātiṣṭhata pāñcālī vāśiteva mahāgajam
english: Reaching the kitchen and finding Bhīmasena, that bright-smiling Pāñcālī stood before him like a white three-year-old cow born in the forest, like a cow in heat before a great elephant.

sanskrit: sā lateva mahāśālaṃ phullaṃ gomatitīrajam bāhubhyāṃ parirabhyainaṃ prābodhayad aninditā siṃhaṃ suptaṃ vane durge mṛgarājavadhūr iva
english: Like a creeper clinging to a great flowering sāla tree on the Gomatī's bank, she embraced him with both arms and awakened him, the blameless one, like a lioness rousing a sleeping lion in a difficult forest.

sanskrit: vīṇeva madhurābhāṣā gāndhāraṃ sādhu mūrcchitā abhyabhāṣata pāñcālī bhīmasenam aninditā
english: With speech sweet as a vīṇā perfectly tuned to the gāndhāra note, that blameless Pāñcālī addressed Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kiṃ śeṣe bhīmasena yathā mṛtaḥ nāmṛtasya hi pāpīyān bhāryām ālabhya jīvati
english: "Rise, rise! Why do you sleep like a dead man, Bhīmasena? A sinful man who is not dead cannot live on after laying hands upon a wife."

sanskrit: tasmiñ jīvati pāpiṣṭhe senāvāhe mama dviṣi tat karma kṛtavaty adya kathaṃ nidrāṃ niṣevase
english: "While that most wicked army commander, my enemy, who has committed such a deed, still lives today — how can you indulge in sleep?"

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāya śayanaṃ rājaputryā prabodhitaḥ upātiṣṭhata meghābhaḥ paryaṅke sopasaṃgrahe
english: Awakened by the princess, he sprang up abandoning his bed, like a cloud in appearance, and sat up on his couch with its cushioned covering.

sanskrit: athābravīd rājaputrīṃ kauravyo mahiṣīṃ priyām kenāsy arthena saṃprāptā tvariteva mamāntikam
english: Then the Kaurava spoke to the princess, his dear wife: "For what purpose have you come to me hastily like this?"

sanskrit: na te prakṛtimān varṇaḥ kṛśā pāṇḍuś ca lakṣyase ācakṣva pariśeṣeṇa sarvaṃ vidyām ahaṃ yathā
english: "Your complexion does not appear natural — you look thin and pale. Tell me everything fully so that I may know it all."

sanskrit: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ dveṣyaṃ vā yadi vā priyam yathāvat sarvam ācakṣva śrutvā jñāsyāmi yat param
english: "Whether it is happiness or suffering, whether hateful or dear — tell me everything accurately; having heard, I will know what further is to be done."

sanskrit: aham eva hi te kṛṣṇe viśvāsyaḥ sarvakarmasu aham āpatsu cāpi tvāṃ mokṣayāmi punaḥ punaḥ
english: "I alone, Kṛṣṇā, am your trusted one in all matters; I too shall rescue you from dangers again and again."

sanskrit: śīghram uktvā yathākāmaṃ yat te kāryaṃ vivakṣitam gaccha vai śayanāyaiva purā nānyo 'vabudhyate
english: "Speak quickly whatever you wish to say, whatever your purpose — then go back to sleep before anyone else becomes aware of it."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca aśocyaṃ nu kutas tasyā yasyā bhartā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ jānan sarvāṇi duḥkhāni kiṃ māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Draupadī said: "How should she not grieve, whose husband is Yudhiṣṭhira — knowing all her sufferings, why do you even ask me?"

sanskrit: yan māṃ dāsīpravādena prātikāmī tadānayat sabhāyāṃ pārṣado madhye tan māṃ dahati bhārata
english: "That the attendant brought me then with the taunt of 'slave-woman,' into the midst of the assembly — that burns me, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: pārthivasya sutā nāma kā nu jīveta mādṛśī anubhūya bhṛśaṃ duḥkham anyatra draupadīṃ prabho
english: "Who else called a king's daughter, like me, could live on after enduring such intense suffering — except Draupadī, O lord?"

sanskrit: vanavāsagatāyāś ca saindhavena durātmanā parāmarśaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca soḍhum utsahate nu kā
english: "And who else could endure to bear the second molestation by the wicked Sindhava while dwelling in forest exile?"

sanskrit: matsyarājñaḥ samakṣaṃ ca tasya dhūrtasya paśyataḥ kīcakena padā spṛṣṭā kā nu jīveta mādṛśī
english: "Touched by Kīcaka's foot in the presence of the Matsya king and before that scoundrel's eyes — who like me could live on?"

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaiḥ kleśaiḥ kliśyamānāṃ ca bhārata na māṃ jānāsi kaunteya kiṃ phalaṃ jīvitena me
english: "Thus afflicted by so many kinds of suffering, O Bhārata, you do not truly know me, O son of Kuntī — what is the fruit of life for me?"

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ rājño virāṭasya kīcako nāma bhārata senānīḥ puruṣavyāghra syālaḥ paramadurmatiḥ
english: "This one, O Bhārata, O tiger among men — the army commander of King Virāṭa named Kīcaka, the king's brother-in-law, of utterly wicked mind —"

sanskrit: sa māṃ sairandhriveṣeṇa vasantīṃ rājaveśmani nityam evāha duṣṭātmā bhāryā mama bhaveti vai
english: "That evil-souled one, while I dwell in the royal palace in the guise of a Sairandhrī, constantly tells me: 'Become my wife.'"

sanskrit: tenopamantryamāṇāyā vadhārheṇa sapatnahan kāleneva phalaṃ pakvaṃ hṛdayaṃ me vidīryate
english: "Being thus solicited by him who deserves death, O slayer of foes, my heart splits like a fruit ripe with time."

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ ca vigarhasva jyeṣṭhaṃ durdyūtadevinam yasyāsmi karmaṇā prāptā duḥkham etad anantakam
english: "And blame your eldest brother, that wicked gambler at dice — through whose action I have obtained this endless suffering."

sanskrit: ko hi rājyaṃ parityajya sarvasvaṃ cātmanā saha pravrajyāyaiva dīvyeta vinā durdyūtadevinam
english: "Who indeed, having abandoned his kingdom and all his possessions along with his own person, would gamble as if in voluntary renunciation — except that wicked dice-player?"

sanskrit: yadi niṣkasahasreṇa yac cānyat sāravad dhanam sāyaṃprātar adeviṣyad api saṃvatsarān bahūn
english: "If he had gambled morning and evening with a thousand niṣkas and with whatever other substantial wealth, even for many years —"

sanskrit: rukmaṃ hiraṇyaṃ vāsāṃsi yānaṃ yugyam ajāvikam aśvāśvatarasaṃghāṃś ca na jātu kṣayam āvahet
english: "Gold, silver, garments, vehicles with their teams, goats and sheep, and herds of horses and mules — none of these would ever have been exhausted."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ dyūtapravādena śriyā pratyavaropitaḥ tūṣṇīm āste yathā mūḍhaḥ svāni karmāṇi cintayan
english: "Yet this same man, stripped of his royal splendour through gambling, sits silent like a fool, pondering his own deeds."

sanskrit: daśa nāgasahasrāṇi padmināṃ hemamālinām yaṃ yāntam anuyāntīha so 'yaṃ dyūtena jīvati
english: "He whom ten thousand lotus-marked elephants, garlanded in gold, used to follow as he went — that same man now lives by gambling."

sanskrit: tathā śatasahasrāṇi nṛṇām amitatejasām upāsate mahārājam indraprasthe yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "Likewise hundreds of thousands of men of boundless splendour used to attend the great king Yudhiṣṭhira at Indraprastha."

sanskrit: śataṃ dāsīsahasrāṇi yasya nityaṃ mahānase pātrīhastaṃ divārātram atithīn bhojayanty uta
english: "A hundred thousand maidservants, with vessels in hand, used to feed guests day and night in his kitchen."

sanskrit: eṣa niṣkasahasrāṇi pradāya dadatāṃ varaḥ dyūtajena hy anarthena mahatā samupāvṛtaḥ
english: "This foremost of givers, who gave away thousands of niṣkas, is now overwhelmed by the great calamity born of gambling."

sanskrit: enaṃ hi svarasaṃpannā bahavaḥ sūtamāgadhāḥ sāyaṃprātar upātiṣṭhan sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ
english: "Many bards and panegyrists, possessed of melodious voices, wearing polished jewelled earrings, used to attend upon him morning and evening."
